newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says indications public finances "serious".
newsitem.headline: Jospin says indications public finances "serious".

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, ordering an audit of public finances to check if France is on course to qualify for the European single currency, said on Thursday the first indications were the situation was serious.
"The first indications given to me allow me to think that the situation of public finances is serious," Jospin told parliament. He did not elaborate. The audit will be completed in mid-July.
Jospin also said he wanted progress towards "a Europe that is more social, a guarantor of progress, peace and independence."

The Socialist leader said his govermnent aimed to stabilise the overall tax burden levied by the state. "If growth allows it, my target is to reduce it in the longer term," he said. An audit of public finances would be completed by mid-July and a corrective supplementary budget put to parliament in the autumn.
The audit expected to how far France has strayed from the aim of reducing its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, a condition for qualifying for the euro currency from 1999.

Jospin, who came to power this month, accused the former centre-right government of covering up the size of the deficit and planning further austerity later this year. Jospin has said he favours the euro but promised during the campaign not to impose extra austerity.
